name: comp-34

frames.best_why: A long entry brings the counter to 46/50 while the field and count are both clear of the cursor.

tagline: A text line with a running character count pinned inside its right edge.
summary: A labelled single-line text field that shows a live character count such as 0/50 inside the right edge and stops accepting input once the limit is reached.
appearance: A label above a rounded dark field on a black stage, with a faint grey counter reading 0/50 pinned inside the right edge. Typed text fills the line from the left and slides under the counter as it grows.
behaviour: Typing fills the line and the counter ticks upward one digit at a time toward 50, after which no more characters are accepted. The clip grows the entry from 0/50 to 46/50 while the line scrolls to keep the caret in view.
demo_content: Label Input with character limit, with a draft ending look great — ship it Friday.
search_phrases: see how many letters are left
limit how much can be typed
use_when: Fields with a hard cap, such as a short bio or status line, where the limit must stay visible.
avoid_when: A single line only; longer text needs a textarea, and the counter shares the same narrow strip.
customise: The label and the 50-character cap are fixed in the file, and the field and counter styling are classes there as well.
weight_why: One field, one counter and a change handler; nothing animates at rest.

a11y.note: The label and live counter are tied to the field with aria-describedby, so the limit is announced as it changes.

issues: The empty field has no placeholder, so nothing hints what the 50 characters are for.
polish_why: Tidy field with a clear live counter, but the demo is a bare text line.
